findings.explanation: Fixed: a CAA record entry was added to the example's records list. The two policies this motivated (SPF permissive-"all", CAA-required) shipped as HLD_GCP_471 and HLD_GCP_472, merged to JamesWoolfenden/holden main. A separate, real engine gap surfaced along the way (each.value-derived for_each attributes always evaluated Unknown, regardless of whether the source list was statically known) and was fixed at the evaluator/parser level (whole-instance fanned-resource synthesis) rather than left as a permanent suppression — verified end-to-end: this module's example now scans with 0 unknown, 0 failed.
findings.title: Example zone has no CAA record restricting certificate issuance for holden-test.example.com.

findings.explanation: Fixed: a DMARC record entry was added to the example's records list. The motivated policy (SPF-requires-DMARC-companion) surfaced a real engine bug along the way: checkCompanion/checkForbidsCompanion unconditionally excluded a candidate whose graph-resource ID matched the subject's — correct for an ordinary resource, but wrong for a for_each-fanned one, where SPF and DMARC are two instances of the *same* records variable collapsing into the *same* google_dns_record_set.records graph node, so the DMARC instance was always excluded as a 'self-match'. Fixed at the evaluator level (self-exclusion now only applies when the resource isn't for_each-fanned). Also simplified the policy itself mid-review: the original where-clause checked both name matches ^_dmarc\. and rrdatas contains v=DMARC1, but name is built via a ternary (endswith(each.value.name, ".") ? ... : "...") rather than a bare each.value.X reference, so it stays unresolvable per-instance regardless of the self-match fix — dropping the name check (rrdatas containing the literal, unambiguous v=DMARC1 tag is already a sufficient signal on its own) sidesteps that gap entirely rather than chasing it. Verified end-to-end: example now scans with 0 unknown, 0 failed.
